newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe pledges to halve budget deficit by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe pledges to halve budget deficit by 2001.

text.p: Zimbabwe said on Thursday it planned to cut its budget deficit to five percent of gross domestic product by 2001 from 11.1 percent at present.
The country has been criticised by the International Monetary Fund and Western economists for its high fiscal deficit, and IMF deputy managing director Alassane Outtara welcomed the move.
State radio quoted Outtara as saying that Zimbabwe's commitment to reducing the deficit meant the IMF would now begin negotiations to resume economic aid for the country's economic policies.
The southern African state would only be able to achieve a halving in the deficit if it cut back its public sector wage and interest bills, he added.
The plans to rein in the deficit were contained in an official paper of long-term forecasts preapred by the government.
